summary.text: Bernadette Greene Placentia, a Democrat and self-described former long-haul truck driver, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Arizona's 8th Congressional District to Abraham Hamadeh.
Born in Galesburg, Illinois, she describes herself as a small-fleet owner who later managed campaigns for other candidates, and as a non-professional politician.

paragraphs.text: Greene Placentia was born in Galesburg, Illinois, and attended the University of Arizona.

She describes a trucking career of more than 27 years and 3.5 million miles as a long-haul driver and small fleet and small business owner, and says that career ended because of economic conditions she attributes to "Bidenomics."
Afterward she worked as a campaign manager for multiple candidates, according to her Candidate Connection survey.
Greene Placentia describes herself as a pro-choice, pro-union, life-long gun owner and "Conservative Democrat" who is not a professional politician.
She won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary for Arizona's 8th District, defeating Raymond Keeler 65.7% to 34.3%, and faced Republican incumbent Abraham Hamadeh in the general election.
Bernadette Greene Placentia lost to Abraham Hamadeh, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
